AIEmotions · transition prototype · iOS 26.5

Motion with
paper weight.

Three directions tested on the daily writing loop and corkboard reading flow. The tactile paper lift fits the product best.

Recommendation · Paper lift
01
Audit

Four seams broke the illusion.

01

Home used one broad implicit animation. The Read action appeared without a staged handoff after saving.

02

The editor arrived as a stock full-screen cover. Its contents had no entrance rhythm.

03

The save/publish card appeared at full opacity and scale. The backdrop and card moved as one flat layer.

04

A note detail replaced the whole corkboard with an edge slide. Readers lost the board as spatial context.

Design rule

Keep the handmade card language in motion. Surfaces should lift, settle, and swap like paper on a desk.

All variants use the same product state and simulator flow. Reduce Motion falls back to a 0.01 s linear change.

02
Direction A · recommended

Paper lift

A soft spring, small vertical travel, and a half-degree rotation make each surface feel picked up by hand.

spring 0.46 / 0.82scale 0.92 → 1y 34 → 0rotation 1.5° → 0°
9.1/10 fit
03
Direction B

Ink bloom

A centered scale and quick fade feel responsive. The motion reads as digital beside the hard shadows and pinned notes.

ease out 0.24 sscale 0.88 → 1center origin
7.4/10 fit
04
Direction C

Quiet slide

Short, restrained travel keeps the words steady. It works for long reading sessions, but the right-edge detail motion feels like navigation instead of handling a note.

ease in/out 0.28 sedge slidelow expression
8.0/10 clarity
05
Comparison

Paper lift keeps context and character.

DirectionProduct fitSpatial clarityCalmUse
Paper liftHighHighMedium-highShip
Ink bloomMediumMediumMediumMicro states
Quiet slideMedium-highHighHighFallback pattern

Decision criteria: match with hard-card visuals, preservation of corkboard context, legibility during text-heavy screens, and motion restraint.

06
Implemented prototype

The seams now share one motion vocabulary.

Changes in the app

Home stages the completed-day scribble and Read reveal after the editor closes. Writing animates its entrance, validation message, backdrop, and confirmation card. Read keeps the board visible behind a dimmed paper detail and animates note replacement.

Debug builds expose all three directions in the existing Testing screen. Release defaults to Paper lift.
